org_1: Hargreaves Grant LLP — mid-size professional services firm specialising in management consulting and technology advisory
org_2: 85 users across finance, HR, project delivery, and business development
org_5: Current system (QuickBooks Enterprise) cannot handle multi-currency, project accounting, or the revenue recognition complexity of the firm's growing international client base. Partner group has mandated a move to a proper professional services ERP.
data_1: Two legacy systems: QuickBooks Enterprise (finance) and a separate timesheet and project tracking tool (Harvest). Both need to be replaced or integrated.
data_2: Basic data audit completed by the Finance Manager. Key findings: 6 years of project financial data in QuickBooks, inconsistent project coding across the two systems, and some client records duplicated between QuickBooks and the CRM (Salesforce).
data_3: Chart of accounts is standardised. Project codes are not — each Partner has used their own naming convention historically.
data_4: 6 years of transactional data. Approximately 340 active projects. 180 active client accounts. Multi-currency — billing in GBP, USD, and EUR.
data_5: GDPR applies. Client confidentiality obligations under consulting engagement contracts. No sector-specific regulatory requirements beyond standard data protection.
proc_1: Finance processes well documented at Level 3. Project accounting processes partially documented. Timesheet and billing processes are informal and vary by Partner.
proc_2: Significant variation in how Partners manage project finances. Some use detailed project budgets; others track informally. Standardisation will be a major change management challenge.
proc_3: Gap analysis completed for finance processes. Not yet completed for project accounting or HR.
proc_4: Partners want flexibility — resistance to rigid standardisation. CFO wants standard Sage Intacct processes where possible to avoid customisation costs.
proc_5: Finance, Project Accounting, Revenue Recognition (ASC 606 / IFRS 15), Billing and Invoicing, Multi-currency, Basic HR and Expenses
people_1: Managing Partner is executive sponsor. Supportive but not hands-on. CFO is the day-to-day champion and is highly engaged.
people_2: Finance Manager identified as internal project lead. Will need external Sage Intacct implementation partner. No dedicated project manager — Finance Manager will run the programme alongside day job.
people_3: Firm has never implemented a major ERP. Previous attempt to implement NetSuite 4 years ago was abandoned after 6 months due to complexity and lack of internal resource.
people_4: No formal change management plan. CFO aware of the failed NetSuite implementation and is keen to do this differently. Plans to hire a part-time Change Manager.
people_5: Partner group is the biggest risk — some Partners are resistant to standardised billing processes and see the ERP as administrative overhead rather than a business tool.
tech_1: Fully cloud-based already — Microsoft 365, Salesforce CRM, Harvest timesheets. No on-premise infrastructure. Sage Intacct is also cloud-based so no infrastructure migration required.
tech_2: Required integrations: Salesforce CRM (opportunity to project conversion), Harvest timesheets (time data into project accounting), payroll (ADP), and expense management (Expensify).
tech_3: IT support is outsourced to a managed service provider. No internal IT team. MSP will need to support the implementation alongside the Sage Intacct partner.
tech_4: No sector-specific regulatory requirements. Standard GDPR data handling. Client data must not be stored outside the UK and EU.
tech_5: No technical architecture review needed — Sage Intacct is SaaS. Integration architecture review required for Salesforce and Harvest connections.
gov_1: Steering committee not yet formed. CFO proposes a committee of Managing Partner, CFO, and two senior Partners. Not yet agreed with the Partner group.
gov_2: Budget approved: £220,000 covering implementation partner, licences, integrations, training, and 15% contingency. Partners have been briefed at a high level only.
gov_3: No risk register started. CFO has a mental list of risks based on the failed NetSuite implementation.
gov_4: 1. Partner resistance to standardised billing processes. 2. Integration complexity with Salesforce and Harvest. 3. Repeat of the NetSuite failure — loss of confidence if the project struggles.
gov_5: No formal benefits plan. CFO expects: elimination of manual Excel consolidation (currently takes 3 days per month), real-time project profitability visibility, and faster client billing cycle (target: from 30 days to 10 days).
